M1a.description: Fold keeps a line-end hyphen before a capital, then lowercases, so a second fold joins the word.
M1a.counterexample: fold('R- M') = 'r- m', but fold('r- m') = 'rm'
M1a.why_this_status: No doc promises that folding twice changes nothing, and the scorer folds each string once, so no verdict can change. The second-fold outcome follows from a documented rule but is not itself documented. The rule: the fold docstring in omni_parse_bench/normalize.py, 'a word broken by a hyphen at a line end -> joined ... when a lowercase letter follows', and the code comment above it, 'only before a lowercase letter, so a line ending "-" before a capital or a digit stays'.
M1a.effect_basis: The scorer folds each string once. Measured on cached leaderboard re-runs (not included here): over the cached re-runs, no already-folded string was folded again, and making fold skip such strings changed no verdict
M1a.who_is_affected: no one today: only a second fold would read these strings differently

M1b.description: Fold keeps a dash at a line end and writes it as '-', so a second fold reads it as a line-end hyphen and joins the word.
M1b.counterexample: fold('y— t') = 'y- t', but fold('y- t') = 'yt'
M1b.why_this_status: No doc promises that folding twice changes nothing, and the scorer folds each string once, so no verdict can change. The second-fold outcome follows from a documented rule but is not itself documented. The rule: the code comment on `_LINE_HYPHEN` in omni_parse_bench/normalize.py, 'Not a dash, which can end a line before a lowercase word', and the fold docstring's typography step, 'dash ... families unified', which writes the kept dash as '-'.
M1b.effect_basis: The scorer folds each string once. Measured on cached leaderboard re-runs (not included here): over the cached re-runs, no already-folded string was folded again, and making fold skip such strings changed no verdict
M1b.who_is_affected: no one today: only a second fold would read these strings differently

M1c.description: Fold turns the elision '[...]' into '[ ]', so a second fold reads it as an unchecked box.
M1c.why_this_status: No doc promises that folding twice changes nothing, and the scorer folds each string once, so no verdict can change. The second-fold outcome follows from the order of fold's documented steps but is not itself documented. The steps: the fold docstring in omni_parse_bench/normalize.py runs 'checkboxes' ('[ ]' -> ☐) before 'leaders' (runs of 3+ dots -> a space), so the '[ ]' that '[...]' leaves is not read as a box until a second fold.
M1c.effect_basis: The scorer folds each string once. Measured on cached leaderboard re-runs (not included here): over the cached re-runs, no already-folded string was folded again, and making fold skip such strings changed no verdict
M1c.who_is_affected: no one today: only a second fold would read these strings differently

M1e.description: Fold removes a bullet only where it starts a line, so in '• •' it removes the first and keeps the second. The second then starts the text, and a second fold removes it too.
M1e.why_this_status: No doc promises that folding twice changes nothing, and the scorer folds each string once. The rule: the fold docstring in omni_parse_bench/normalize.py, 'a bullet glyph starting a line -> a space'; docs/scoring/internals.md (Fold, case fold-bullet) shows a bullet inside a line kept.
M1e.effect_basis: not measured: it was not re-scored on cached leaderboard re-runs, and this package holds no system outputs to measure it with. The scorer folds each string once, and no real text string folds differently twice this way
M1e.who_is_affected: no one seen: only a second fold reads these strings differently

M2e.description: Fold reads the case of the letter after a line-end hyphen, so the upper and lower case of the same words can fold differently.
M2e.counterexample: fold('RE- M') = 're- m', but fold('re- m') = 'rem'
M2e.why_this_status: The fold docstring in omni_parse_bench/normalize.py joins a line-end hyphen only 'when a lowercase letter follows'; docs/scoring/order.md (case ord-case-hyphen) shows 'R- M' not found in 'r- m'.
M2e.effect_basis: not measured: it was not re-scored on cached leaderboard re-runs, and this package holds no system outputs to measure it with. The 18 real tests it touches are listed, so it can change their verdicts
M2e.how_common: 18 real tests: those with a line-end hyphen that fail on their answer in another case
M2e.who_is_affected: a page that writes such a line in another case than the gold (for example a heading in capitals) fails the test

M11b.description: Only present accepts a hyphenated word broken after its hyphen. Order, repeat and table_cell fold 'aa- bb' to 'aabb', whether the page or the gold holds the break.
M11b.counterexample:
Order('aa-bb', 'tail') fails on `

aa-
bb

tail

`. The reverse also fails: Order('self- aware', 'tail') on `

self-aware

tail

`, while present passes both
M11b.why_this_status: The label covers the direction this relation tests: a page that breaks the word. The docstring of omni_parse_bench/scorers/unit_tests/hyphenation.py says 'Only text presence uses this fallback', and docs/scoring/internals.md (The hyphen rule, cases hyph-order, hyph-repeat, hyph-cell) shows those three tests failing. The reverse direction, a gold that holds the broken word ('self- aware') against a page that writes 'self-aware', also passes present and fails the other three. It follows from fold joining a line-end hyphen in every string, the gold's included (docs/scoring/internals.md, The hyphen rule). It is an artefact in the gold, not a verdict the docs promise.
M11b.effect_basis: Measured on cached leaderboard re-runs (not included here): extending the hyphen fallback to order, repeat and table_cell would change the verdict of a handful of tests, all from fail to pass. Both directions occur. In most the gold holds the broken word: a correct page failed because of an artefact in the gold
M11b.how_common: Measured on cached leaderboard re-runs (not included here): a handful of tests
M11b.who_is_affected: a page that breaks a hyphenated word after its hyphen fails order, repeat and table_cell tests of that word (present accepts it); and a correct page fails those tests when the gold holds the broken word

M15b.description: Fold lowercases and does not casefold, so a letter whose upper case lowers to other letters is lost.
M15b.why_this_status: The fold docstring in omni_parse_bench/normalize.py says 'lowercased'; docs/scoring/internals.md (Fold, case fold-case: 'no letter is changed into others') shows 'STRASSE' and 'straße' folding apart.
M15b.effect_basis: not measured: it was not re-scored on cached leaderboard re-runs, and this package holds no system outputs to measure it with. The 15 real tests it touches are listed, so it can change their verdicts
M15b.how_common: 15 real tests: 12 in polytonic Greek, 2 with dotless ı, 1 with ß
M15b.who_is_affected: a page that writes such a word in upper case fails a test whose gold is in lower case

M16.description: When two blocks with the same box hold a place, the first listed decides the verdict.
M16.counterexample: a text test passes on blocks [text, heading] with one box and fails on [heading, text]
M16.why_this_status: docs/scoring/layout_kind.md: the holder is the smallest covering block, 'on equal areas, the first listed' (case lay-tie); `holder` in omni_parse_bench/scorers/unit_tests/runners.py keeps the first listed of the blocks whose areas are equal within `AREA_EPS`.
M16.effect_basis: not measured: it was not re-scored on cached leaderboard re-runs, and this package holds no system outputs to measure it with
M16.how_common: not measured: counting it needs system outputs (their blocks), which this package does not hold
M16.who_is_affected: an output listing two blocks with one box and different labels: their order decides

M22b.description: A line-end hyphen joins across a paragraph break, so a text test that ends in a hyphen fails once the next paragraph starts with a lowercase letter.
M22b.counterexample:
Text('well-') passes on `

well-

` and fails on `

well-

known

`: fold reads the page as 'wellknown'.
M22b.why_this_status: The scorer does this on purpose: docs/scoring/internals.md (Fold) says that for a line-end hyphen a block break is a line break like any other, which outputs that write one paragraph per printed line rely on (case fold-hyphen-block), and the comment on `_LINE_HYPHEN` in omni_parse_bench/normalize.py says the same. A leader run does stop at a block break (M22a).
M22b.effect_basis: Measured on cached leaderboard re-runs (not included here): stopping the join at a paragraph break failed order tests on correct pages that write one paragraph per printed line and break a word there ('Head-' then 'quarters'), so the join was kept. What the join itself costs, a text that ends in a hyphen before a lowercase paragraph, was not measured on its own.
M22b.how_common: The real tests hold 2 text strings and 3 order strings that end in a letter and a hyphen (counted with a pattern match). How often a page puts a lowercase paragraph right after one was not measured
M22b.who_is_affected: a text test that ends in a hyphen (a word the gold keeps broken at a printed line end), on a page that puts the rest of the word in the next paragraph

M23a.description: Present forgives inserted letters, and some deleted ones: j letters inserted into the text, or deleted from a page that holds only the text, or deleted at the text's end, can pass with a budget below j. Two more forms: a text that starts or ends the page text gets about 1.5 times its budget for substituted letters, and a letter moved a few places costs one edit.
M23a.counterexample: Text('lorem ipsum dolor sit amet', k) passes on 'lorem izpsum dolqor sit amjet' (3 letters inserted) from k = 2, and on 'lorem ipsum dolor sit' (5 characters deleted at the end) from k = 3. Text('lorem ipsum', 2) passes on 'abc xxxem ipsum' (the text ends the page, its first 3 letters substituted) and fails on 'abc xxxem ipsum dolor'. Text('abcdefgh', 1) passes on 'zz acdebfgh zz' (b moved 3 places: edit distance 2)
M23a.why_this_status: The scorer's docs promise a budget of edits: docs/scoring/present-text.md says present allows 'up to `max_diffs` character edits'; in omni_parse_bench/scorers/unit_tests/runners.py the `_ratio` docstring says it 'passes when the best partial match is within `max_diffs` edits', and the comment on `EPS` says 'rapidfuzz returns exactly that ratio for k edits'. That holds for substituted letters (M3), not for inserted ones: rapidfuzz's partial ratio scores an inserted letter as less than one edit. docs/scoring/internals.md (The edit budget) states the inserted and deleted letters measured here. It names swapped letters too, but not a text at the edge of the page text, nor a moved letter.
M23a.effect_basis: Measured on cached leaderboard re-runs (not included here): counting edits exactly would fail a small share of the tests that carry a budget, all of them pages that sit one edit or more over it, and none the other way. The budgets were set against the measure the scorer uses, so the published scores include this forgiveness and an exact count would lower them
M23a.how_common: 1,370 of the 3,684 real present text tests carry a max_diffs of 1 or more (counted when the dataset is set); the others have no edit to spend
M23a.who_is_affected: text tests with max_diffs 1 or more: a page that adds letters inside the text, drops letters at its end, misreads letters where the text starts or ends the page text, or moves a letter, can pass with more edits than the test allows

M23b.description: Table_cell compares whole cells by a ratio over both lengths, so an inserted or deleted letter costs about half an edit: j such letters can pass with a budget below j.
M23b.counterexample: TableCell('lorem ipsum dolor sit amet', k) passes on the cell 'lorem izpsum dolzor sit amzet' (3 letters inserted) from k = 2
M23b.why_this_status: docs/scoring/internals.md (The edit budget) says table_cell 'compares whole cells with a ratio over both lengths, so an inserted character costs half an edit', and docs/scoring/table_cell.md lists it as a blind spot (case cell-insertions: the output is wrong but passes). A deleted letter costs about half an edit by the same ratio; the docs say so in words for insertions only.
M23b.effect_basis: not measured: it was not re-scored on cached leaderboard re-runs, and this package holds no system outputs to measure it with. It can only turn a fail into a pass: no cell within its budget failed in these checks, and only the 62 tests with a budget can be affected
M23b.how_common: 62 of the 5,386 real table_cell tests carry a max_diffs of 1 or more (counted when the dataset is set); the others have no edit to spend
M23b.who_is_affected: table_cell tests with max_diffs 1 or more: a cell with extra or missing letters can pass with more edits than the test allows
